STEP 1 - Vessel type: shallow-to-medium bowl (white, curved inner wall visible, food sits near the rim). Classified as a serving/salad bowl.

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type cue: a salad bowl is typically 20-25 cm.
b) Reference cue: the avocado slices are about 8-9 cm long, and the bowl spans roughly 2.5-3 avocado lengths across. That gives about 22-24 cm.
Final width: about 23 cm.

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Bowl capacity: 0.2 x 23^3 / 1000 = 2.43 L (taking the shallow-bowl formula, since the food is not deep).
- Fill: the food mound sits roughly level with or slightly above the rim, so fill ≈ 0.9.
- Food volume: 2.43 x 0.9 x 0.9 ≈ 1.97 L ≈ 1970 ml. Note this is a gross estimate; the greens and gaps reduce the true solid volume, so I'll apply the split by item shares.

Item shares (visual estimate by surface coverage and depth):
- Chicken breast (cubed, cooked): about 40% → ~790 g at 1.0 g/ml ... adjusted down for air gaps to ~400 g.
- Avocado: about 25% → ~200 g.
- Mixed raw greens (spinach/arugula): about 20% → ~120 g at 0.15 g/ml on a large volume share, adjusted to ~150 g.
- Broccoli florets: about 10% → ~60 g.
- Light dressing/oil: about 5% → ~15 g.

Adjusted totals (gaps and air reduce the solid mass): chicken ~150 g, avocado ~100 g, greens ~60 g, broccoli ~30 g, dressing ~10 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: the greens form a base layer under the chicken and avocado, already counted above.

STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g (as served):
- Cooked chicken breast: 165 kcal
- Avocado: 160 kcal
- Mixed raw greens: 23 kcal
- Broccoli (cooked/steamed): 35 kcal
- Oil/light dressing: 300 kcal (approximate)

Total: about 150 g chicken (~248 kcal) + 100 g avocado (~160 kcal) + 60 g greens (~14 kcal) + 30 g broccoli (~11 kcal) + 10 g dressing (~30 kcal) ≈ 463 kcal, roughly 350 g total.
